result.summary: REQ-511 / GH #2682 PR b implemented per lib/letflow/design/req511-exam-content-snapshot.md (13 PR b row, 17.2, 17.6, 18.5, 18.6): certificate path reads facts only from the session snapshot (Session.get_snapshot_for_user/3 + Snapshot.certificate_facts/1; late_certificate facts for legacy submitted sessions); lazy late snapshot at first touch for in_progress sessions (Snapshot.ensure/3 for state/autosave, ensure_locked/2 + record_late/4 for submit/finalize) with the exam.session_snapshot_late hash-chained audit entry in the same transaction; Snapshot.cutover/1 compared against the session record's server-set inserted_at; Stamp per-tenant prerequisites + active-row compatibility + prerequisites_missing/gate_blocked_total; config :exam_snapshot_complete flipped false -> true in config/config.exs (test.exs already true); Snapshot.late_origin_counts/1; certificate render clauses. No tests written (TEST-DESIGNER). Not committed or pushed.

deviations: D-b1: Snapshot.ensure_locked/2 returns {:ok, snapshot, session_after, provenance} (provenance :existing | :late) and for :late only BUILDS (reads); it does not write. The caller (score_and_persist) persists session_after.field_values in its ONE existing session update after persist_scores, then calls Snapshot.record_late/4 (audit) as the last statement. Reason: the design's order (write the session snapshot first, then score) takes the session-type sequence lock before the score-type sequence lock, the reverse of a plain submit (scores first, then session update), so a late submit concurrent with a plain submit of another session could deadlock (session-seq <-> score-seq cycle). The deferred write keeps the plain-submit order and puts the audit chain lock last. Still exactly one ENTITY_RECORD_UPDATED event adds exam_snapshot (I-2). Ensure/3 (state/autosave touch) and ensure_certificate_facts/3 write immediately: session row -> session sequence -> audit.
D-b2: Snapshot.build_from_resolved/4 accepts origin :start | :late (build_late reuses it); build_info type widened.

D-b3: Snapshot.ensure/ensure_certificate_facts return an already-present snapshot (verified) BEFORE probing prerequisites; prerequisites (definition/restriction, then cutover) are probed only when the snapshot is absent and the status is eligible (in_progress / submitted). Non-owner and nonexistent still stop after the single lock query, before any probe (18.6). A terminal snapshotless session returns :snapshot_missing without probing.

D-b4: Snapshot.check_prerequisites/1 (was private Session.check_snapshot_prerequisites) is now public in Snapshot and used by both the start path and the late path; the three private helpers were deleted from session.ex; the unused Definitions alias was removed from session.ex.

D-b5: Stamp prerequisites are checked only for a REAL run and only when the tenant still has an unstamped (managed_by NULL) row, advisory pre-pass AND again under the row locks (rollback {:prerequisites_missing, list}); a fully stamped tenant stays :nothing_to_stamp; dry run never blocked. Answer-key pairs come from Catalog.fetch("exam") -> exam.answer_key_fields() (no Exam module literal, boundary rule 5).
D-b6: Design text says 'six' answer_key_fields pairs; code (and PR a) has five (4 existing + session.exam_snapshot). The prerequisite uses whatever answer_key_fields/0 returns.
D-b7: verify/0 needed no PR b addition (the PR a shape of 17.2 already covers session_definition + answer_key_restrictions; Stamp reuses the same two prerequisites).
config flag: config/config.exs line 67 was already `false` (PR a) and is flipped to `true` here; config/test.exs already `true` (unchanged). The single flip per 10.1/18.3.

inserted_at_evidence.compared_quantity: entity_record_latest.inserted_at of the session RECORD (Letflow.Entities.Record.Latest struct, column from `timestamps(type: :utc_datetime_usec)` at record/latest.ex:35), compared in Snapshot.check_before_cutover/2, never the started_at field
inserted_at_evidence.entity_record_latest_path: records.ex upsert_record_latest/3 (:create at ~857) inserts via Latest.insert_changeset whose cast list @insert_fields = [:entity_type, :record_id, :field_values, :entity_def_version, :last_event_global_seq] (latest.ex ~38-44) excludes inserted_at, so it is Ecto-autogenerated server-side on insert; the :update/:delete clause (~873) uses Latest.update_changeset whose cast list @update_fields = [:field_values, :deleted, :entity_def_version, :last_event_global_seq] (latest.ex ~46) excludes inserted_at (and the changeset only touches updated_at via autogen). So the update never rewrites inserted_at.
inserted_at_evidence.promoted_table_path: records.ex build_upsert_sql (~1107): `update_columns = all_columns -- ["id", "record_id", "inserted_at"]`, so ON CONFLICT (record_id) DO UPDATE SET never includes inserted_at.
inserted_at_evidence.note: The promoted per-type table also has its own inserted_at (INSERT only); the cutover compares the entity_record_latest one that Session/Snapshot read via Latest.

lock_order_evidence.order: exam row (create only) -> session row (FOR UPDATE) -> entity-type instance sequence lock (Records write) -> audit chain lock (last)
lock_order_evidence.new_callers_of_audit: the only new Audit.insert_entry call is Snapshot.record_late/4 (snapshot.ex ~867); its three call sites: snapshot.ex:711 (ensure/3, after write_session at :710, last statement of the transaction), snapshot.ex:1020 (ensure_certificate_facts/3, after write_session at :1019, last), session.ex:1334 (score_and_persist/3, after persist_scores and update_session_after_submit, last).
lock_order_evidence.submit_late_path: lock_session_row (session.ex:672/711) -> Snapshot.ensure_locked (reads only, no sequence lock, no audit) -> persist_scores (score sequence) -> update_session_after_submit (session sequence) -> record_late (audit chain). Plain submit: session row -> score sequence -> session sequence. Same order, audit appended at the end.
lock_order_evidence.grep: grep -rn 'Snapshot\.\|lock_exam_row\|lock_session_row' lib/letflow shows the session/exam row locks and Snapshot callers only inside lib/letflow/modules/exam/* (plus authorization.ex/release/exam_snapshot.ex references that take no lock); grep -rn 'Audit.insert_entry' lib shows no other caller that later takes a session row, exam row or session/score sequence lock: Stamp.audit!/4 (stamp.ex ~384) runs after the definition row locks and is the last statement before the setting reset (holds no session/exam row lock); engine/identity/definitions callers do not touch exam session rows. No path takes the audit chain lock and then a session row, exam row or instance sequence lock.
lock_order_evidence.nonowner_parity: ensure/3 and ensure_certificate_facts/3: lock query (1 statement) then owner check; autosave/state stop at fetch_session+check_owner before any ensure; nonexistent -> :session_not_found after the same single query.

notes_for_test_designer: Legacy-session fixtures: fixtures carry exam_snapshot from install so every plain session is AFTER the cutover; use ONE legacy_session! helper that removes exam_snapshot from field_values via a test-support write, sets entity_record_latest.inserted_at earlier than Snapshot.cutover(prefix), started_at earlier, expires_at in the future (T-21..T-25, T-48..T-52, T-58, T-59, T-63). T-61/T-61b use a session whose record inserted_at is >= cutover with started_at set far in the past.

ensure_locked/2 does NOT write (D-b1): T-59 should assert the returned session_after.field_values carries the snapshot and that after a submit the persisted session still carries it; T-58 (audit entry count, audit failure rollback -> {:snapshot_error, :audit_failed}) is observable through ensure/3, ensure_certificate_facts/3 and Session.submit/finalize_expired. Audit failure can be provoked by e.g. a tenant whose audit chain insert fails; the whole transaction (snapshot write, scores, status) rolls back, session stays in_progress.

T-24 (concurrent touches): second toucher sees the snapshot after the lock and does not write; exactly one ENTITY_RECORD_UPDATED event adds exam_snapshot and exactly one exam.session_snapshot_late audit entry.

T-63 query parity: ensure/3 and ensure_certificate_facts/3 execute lock query then owner check only for a non-owner/nonexistent session; autosave and state read return at fetch_session/check_owner. Measure with a repo telemetry counter.

Snapshot.cutover/1 unit (T-63b): MIN activated_at over artifact_activation_history rows (artifact_kind :entity, artifact_name 'session') whose new_version_id matches an entity_definitions row (tenant, name 'session') whose definition_json contains field name 'exam_snapshot'; {:error, :definition_missing} when none.
Snapshot.late_origin_counts/1 -> {:ok, %{late: n, late_certificate: n}} counts non-deleted session records by exam_snapshot.origin; {:error, :invalid_schema_name} for a bad prefix.

Session.get_snapshot_for_user/3: present snapshot -> fetch_verified (corrupt -> {:grading_error, :snapshot_corrupt}); absent + submitted -> ensure_certificate_facts; absent + other status -> {:grading_error, :snapshot_missing}, no write. Certificate guard order: grading_pending -> not submitted -> snapshot facts -> exam_not_certifiable -> not passed -> issue; exam_title comes from the snapshot.

Stamp: prerequisites_missing order is [:session_definition, :answer_key_restrictions]; judged row = :active row else newest by inserted_at; T-40: old inactive version without the field plus new active version with it is stampable and all rows get managed_by.

Router: certificate and download render {:grading_error, _} as 500 with detail 'exam grading failed; the session was not scored' and {:snapshot_error, _} as 503 'exam service is being upgraded; retry shortly' (existing render_snapshot_failure/4), logged with route tags certificate / certificate_download.
notes_for_pr_body: Infra rollout already ran on QA after a5847f1ff (1 tenant upgraded). Any OTHER environment receiving a5847f1ff or later needs Letflow.Release.ExamSnapshot.rollout/1 run (bin/letflow rpc "IO.inspect(Letflow.Release.ExamSnapshot.rollout(dry_run: false))") and Letflow.Release.ExamSnapshot.verify() to report ready: true before any managed-type stamp; with this PR a real Letflow.Release.ManagedTypes.stamp/1 additionally refuses (status :snapshot_prerequisite_missing) any tenant not rolled out.
Ordering: rollout first, then stamp. This PR flips :exam_snapshot_complete to true; it does not stamp anything.
Late snapshots are audited (action exam.session_snapshot_late); post-deploy count via Letflow.Modules.Exam.Snapshot.late_origin_counts/1.
